per_question.question: Are there quantity limits on prescription drugs under NC Medicaid, and when is prior authorization required for pharmacy claims?
per_question.agent_answer:
I’m going to pull the pharmacy policy sections that address quantity limits and prior authorization criteria/process, then I’ll verify whether the underlying policy has any amendments that change those rules.I found the main pharmacy policy: Clinical Coverage Policy 9. The search also surfaced a dedicated “Prior Approval Drugs and Criteria” section and a quantity-limits section, so I’m going to read those full sections and the document structure next.The dedicated PA-drug section is mostly a list of drug classes, while the process attachment explains what happens when a claim hits a PA edit. I still need the core policy language on when PA is required and whether quantity limits apply generally, so I’m pulling the document outline and any amendments now.I now have the document structure and confirmed the current authoritative document is the July 15, 2024 version of Policy 9. Next I’m reading the core coverage and PA sections so I can answer the “are there limits?” and “when is PA required?” parts from the actual text, not just headings.**Yes — NC Medicaid pharmacy claims can be subject to quantity limits, and prior authorization is required when a drug is on NC Medicaid’s prior-approval list or when the claim hits a PA-related edit.**

## Short answer

- **Quantity limits exist.** Clinical Coverage Policy 9 includes a section titled **“Quantity and Episodic Drugs,”** which expressly refers to **“quantity limitations of episodic drugs”** and to **“prior authorization criteria and requirements.”** It does **not** state in the retrieved text that *all* drugs have one uniform quantity cap; instead, it confirms that NC Medicaid applies quantity limitations for at least some drugs/drug categories.  
  **Citation:** Clinical Coverage Policy 9, Section 5.4.3 — “Quantity and Episodic Drugs” ([Lock-in Program](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/9-outpatient-pharmacy-program/download?attachment)), effective July 15, 2024.

- **Prior authorization is required when the drug is subject to NC Medicaid prior-approval criteria.** Policy 9 contains a dedicated section titled **“Pharmacy Prior Approval Drugs and Criteria”** listing many drug classes/products subject to PA criteria, including examples like GLP-1 receptor agonists, hepatitis C medications, growth hormones, PCSK9 inhibitors, Synagis, CGM systems/supplies, certain opioids, and others.  
  **Citation:** Clinical Coverage Policy 9 — “Pharmacy Prior Approval Drugs and Criteria” ([Lock-in Program](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/9-outpatient-pharmacy-program/download?attachment)), effective July 15, 2024.

## When PA is required for a pharmacy claim

From the text I retrieved, the clearest operational rule is:

- If the prescriber **has not obtained prior authorization**, the point-of-sale system will return one of these messages:
  - **“PA REQ. PRESCRIBER CALL CSC”**
  - **“CLAIM DENIED. PA LIMITS EXCEEDED.”**  
  **Citation:** Clinical Coverage Policy 9, Attachment C — “Requesting Prior Authorization for Prescription Drugs” ([Lock-in Program](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/9-outpatient-pharmacy-program/download?attachment)), effective July 15, 2024.

That means, in practice, **PA is required before payment whenever the claim is for a drug/edit that NC Medicaid has placed under prior approval or quantity-limit controls and the claim cannot pass at POS without that approval.**

## Who has to request the PA

- **The prescriber** contacts the clinical call center/NCTracks **online, by telephone, or by fax** to request PA.  
- If approved, the system is updated and the pharmacy can then submit the claim.  
  **Citation:** Clinical Coverage Policy 9, Attachment C — “Requesting Prior Authorization for Prescription Drugs” ([Lock-in Program](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/9-outpatient-pharmacy-program/download?attachment)).

## What I can say confidently from the policy text

### 1) Are there quantity limits?
**Yes.** The policy expressly references:
- **“quantity limitations of episodic drugs”**
- **“prior authorization criteria and requirements”**
- efforts to minimize dispensing fees for drugs prescribed in limited quantities  
**Citation:** Clinical Coverage Policy 9, Section 5.4.3 — “Quantity and Episodic Drugs” ([Lock-in Program](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/9-outpatient-pharmacy-program/download?attachment)).

### 2) Does every prescription require PA?
**No.** The policy’s covered-drug section shows many prescription drugs are covered if they meet general criteria, while PA applies to selected drugs/classes subject to NC Medicaid’s prior-approval rules.  
**Citation:** Clinical Coverage Policy 9, Section 3.2.1 — “Specific criteria covered by Medicaid” ([Lock-in Program](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/9-outpatient-pharmacy-program/download?attachment)); Clinical Coverage Policy 9 — “Pharmacy Prior Approval Drugs and Criteria” ([Lock-in Program](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/9-outpatient-pharmacy-program/download?attachment)).

### 3) What happens at the pharmacy counter if PA is needed?
The POS system returns a PA-required or limits-exceeded denial message, and the pharmacy is told to have the **prescriber** complete the PA if it has not already been done.  
**Citation:** Clinical Coverage Policy 9, Attachment C — “Requesting Prior Authorization for Prescription Drugs” ([Lock-in Program](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/9-outpatient-pharmacy-program/download?attachment)).

## Important limit on what I could confirm

I **could not find in the retrieved text** a single section that states a universal numeric quantity limit for all outpatient drugs, or a clean sentence like “PA is required whenever quantity limits are exceeded.” The policy sections I retrieved show that:

- quantity limits **do exist** for some drugs;
- PA criteria **do exist** for selected drugs/classes; and
- claims will deny with PA-related messages when prior approval has not been obtained or PA limits are exceeded.

But I did **not** retrieve the exact drug-by-drug quantity-limit tables or the detailed criteria pages for each medication/class. So I should **not** state specific day-supply caps, refill limits, or unit limits unless I pull the exact drug-specific criteria.

## Bottom line

**NC Medicaid does impose pharmacy quantity limits for at least some drugs, and prior authorization is required when the drug or claim falls under NC Medicaid’s prior-approval criteria or quantity-limit edits at POS.** The prescriber—not the pharmacy—must request the PA through NCTracks/CSC, and without it the claim may return **“PA REQ. PRESCRIBER CALL CSC”** or **“CLAIM DENIED. PA LIMITS EXCEEDED.”**

I checked the current Policy 9 document and found the current authoritative version is effective **July 15, 2024**. If you want, I can next pull the **drug-specific prior approval criteria/quantity-limit source** for a particular medication or class (for example GLP-1s, opioids, CGMs, hepatitis C drugs, etc.) and tell you the exact trigger.
